title: Collocation and lexical gaps
summary: Retrieve a content word or fixed expression by combining the surrounding word partnership with the passage meaning.

sections.title: Recall words as partners
content: Complete these familiar partnerships aloud: make a decision, take charge, pay attention, play a role and reach an agreement.

A lexical gap usually needs a word with enough meaning to name an action, object, quality or idea. Grammar narrows the word class, but the words beside the gap often decide which natural partnership fits.

sections.title: Use the frame–meaning–cohesion routine
content: Read the frame around the gap. Preserve small words such as at, of, on and to because they may form part of a fixed expression.
Name the intended meaning in plain language. Ask what action, object or idea the sentence must express before retrieving a word.
Check cohesion across the paragraph. Characters, events, contrasts and consequences can rule out a locally grammatical guess.
Test naturalness by rereading the complete phrase. A synonym can match the dictionary meaning yet fail to combine naturally with its neighbours.

sections.title: Choose the established combination
content: In “the booking changed at short ___”, the frame at short and the meaning with little warning retrieve notice: at short notice.
In “Mei agreed to take ___ of the schedule”, the frame take ___ of and the meaning accept responsibility retrieve charge.
In “the rehearsal came to a ___”, the frame came to a and the interrupted action allow halt; stop is also natural and must be explicitly approved if accepted.
In “the group played a crucial ___”, the adjective crucial, the verb played and the group's contribution retrieve role; part is an approved equivalent in this frame.

sections.title: Separate possible from natural
content: For each gap, bracket the full phrase rather than reading only the word immediately before the blank. Label its intended meaning in three or four words.
Generate no more than two candidates. Insert each one, reread the whole sentence and reject any choice that breaks the fixed frame, paragraph meaning or register.

sections.title: Restore a rehearsal narrative
content: Read all three paragraphs of “The rehearsal rescue”. Enter exactly one word in each of the eight gaps to complete a common collocation or fixed expression.
Do not submit after solving only the obvious phrases. Use the team's problem, response and result to check that every completed expression supports the same narrative.

sections.title: Diagnose the lexical error
content: Frame error: I ignored a preposition, determiner or nearby word that belongs to the fixed expression.
Meaning error: I chose a natural phrase, but it expressed the wrong action or relationship in this passage.
Synonym trap: I chose a word with a similar dictionary meaning that does not combine naturally with the surrounding words.
Cohesion error: I solved the sentence alone and missed what the preceding or following sentence established. Record the closest cause before retrying.

sections.title: The rehearsal rescue
content: Complete one original eight-gap narrative using common collocations and fixed expressions. Feedback appears only after the whole passage is submitted, and only explicitly reviewed alternatives receive credit.
